title: Sale Banner Maker for Square Offer Images | AIVideosUGC
description: Move stock with a sale image that leaves clean space for your offer. One product photo becomes a square banner; add the discount and dates yourself.
h1: Sale Banner Maker with Room for the Offer
lead: A discount with no clear product image disappears in the feed. This sale banner maker turns one product photo into a square scene with a calm area for the offer you add later.
steps_h2: Make a Sale Banner in 3 Steps
steps_lead: Upload the product, leave an open area, then add the real offer after download.

steps.d: Start with one clear photo of the sale product, full item in frame. The scene comes from that photo, not from a typed discount.
Describe the setting and say you want a calm open area. Leave the percentage, code and end date out of the generation.
Add the confirmed discount, code and end date in your editor, then post. Read every figure on a phone preview first.

faq.q: Why doesn't the banner include my discount text?
faq.a: Generated lettering can garble words and digits, and a wrong price on a sale ad is a real problem. Add the offer yourself so every figure matches the promotion you approved.

faq.q: What size is the sale image?
faq.a: Square by default, which fits a Facebook or Instagram feed post. For a wide website header, place the image on a wider canvas in your design tool.

faq.q: Can I reuse one scene for a different offer?
faq.a: Yes. Add the offer as text after download, so the same scene can carry a percent-off line in one ad and a different approved line in another.

faq.q: Can I make a vertical sale story from it?
faq.a: The template produces a square image. If you need a Story or Reel frame, put that square on a 9:16 canvas after download.

faq.q: Where should the discount code go?
faq.a: Put the code in the open area as editable text, then read the full offer on a phone-sized preview. Do not ask the generator to paint the code into the photo.

faq.q: How many credits does a sale photo use?
faq.a: Each photo costs 24 credits, the cost is shown before you start, and a failed job returns those credits. The download has no watermark, and you can use it in your own ads, pages and posts. You are responsible for the offer terms and the disclosures in the ad.

faq.q: What happens when the sale ends?
faq.a: Delete, pause or replace the offer layer so an old date or code is never shown. The product scene can stay for a later promotion or as a plain listing image.

faq.q: Can I start from a Black Friday scene and change the holiday later?
faq.a: Yes. Keep the product scene and swap the headline. Seasonal campaign notes live on [Black Friday ad creatives](page:occ-black-friday).

reviews.h2: Sale Scenes Sellers Build from One Photo
reviews.lead: A few ways sellers use one product photo as the scene behind an offer.

items.d: The shop generates a seasonal scene and types the percent, code and end date in its editor. When the number changes, the text layer changes and the product scene can stay.

items.t: End date kept out of the file
items.d: The end date is not generated into the image, so an expired promotion is removed by deleting the text layer. The product photo underneath can be reused.
The same scene carries a percent-off line in one ad and a different approved line in another. Both lines are added after download.
A calm area is left for the code, then checked on a phone-sized preview before the ad is published. The generated file has no digits in it.
The square image goes in a Facebook or Instagram feed, or on the product page, after the final offer is added. A wide site header means placing it on a wider canvas in the editor.

items.t: No new shoot for the event
items.d: They start from a product photo they already have instead of booking a banner shoot. Claims and offer terms stay their responsibility.
